theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners rank 1 with the highest score (1.8), strongest durability_bar (0.66), and breadth 0.933 — the one theme with both leadership and shallow-but-broad participation. It is eligible under the absolute-trend gate, which is this market's only validated leg (drawdown/shake-out avoidance, not return forecasting). The lean expresses a trend-following, vol-aware stay with the confirmed leader, not a momentum-buy call.
evidence: durability_bar 0.66, breadth 0.933 (cohesion is high relative to the field)

gate_helps=true — absolute-trend discipline is the validated risk-control leg
theses.dissent: hurst_tag is 'mixed' (not clean trending), and r10 is −0.0054 — near-term momentum is already flagging; the high breadth may mark late-stage participation rather than durable leadership, and precious-metals leadership can reverse on a risk-on sentiment shift or USD strength.

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties is the adjacent challenger (rank 2, score 1.627, eligible) with breadth 0.917 and the same eligible trend-gate profile as the leader. It is the coherent second leg of the precious-metals complex; leaning with it keeps exposure on the same confirmed leadership cluster without predicting a handoff to it.
evidence: rotational margin to leader is only 0.173 — no confirmed handoff, just nearby complex strength

theses.dissent: Silver is higher-beta than gold, so a precious-metals shakeout would hit it harder; the shared ETF proxy (XGD.TO) with Gold Miners means the two theses are not independent — if the complex rolls over, both fail together.

It is a clear confirmed-laggard with evidence of trend degeneration; the only validated use of the trend gate is to avoid staying-power risk in names that have broken trend.
evidence: hurst_tag 'trend' with breadth near zero — a down-trend with no internal support
gate_helps=true — the validated edge is staying OUT of broken-trend themes
theses.dissent: Utilities are rate-sensitive and defensive; a sharp risk-off or a bond-yield reversal could quickly flip this theme into a relative haven, and a mean-reversion in the crowded-short complex would punish an underweight bias just as easily.
